paragraphs.source_en: When word came that Hashiba Hideyoshi’s reinforcements had arrived, Shibata Katsuie could not help cursing, “Damn fool!” Yet the curse was not directed at Hideyoshi. paragraphs.source_en: Had Katsuie been thinking then of the greater cause—of staking his life upon it here—he might not have been so lost. But what swelled within him was not the greater cause; it was glory. Why could he not submit to that greater cause, devote himself to ending the fires of war in this age of chaos, and willingly yield to Hideyoshi? Why was he so obstinate?
